datasets.name: emg2pose: Surface EMG and Hand Pose
datasets.description: This dataset is a NEMAR re-host and BIDS conversion of the emg2pose benchmark, comprising surface electromyography (EMG) recordings paired with hand pose labels for wrist-worn sEMG-based hand pose estimation. It includes 16-channel, 2 kHz sEMG recordings synchronized with joint-angle labels derived from a 26-camera motion-capture rig, spanning 193 users, 370 hours, and approximately 80 million labeled frames across 29 behavioral stages.
datasets.authors: Sasha Salter, Richard Warren, Collin Schlager, Adrian Spurr, Shangchen Han, Rohin Bhasin, Yujun Cai, Peter Walkington, Anuoluwapo Bolarinwa, Robert Wang, Nathan Danielson, Josh Merel, Eftychios Pnevmatikakis, Jesse Marshall, Alexandre Gramfort

datasets.name: BCCWJ-MEG
datasets.description: This dataset comprises magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 35 Japanese native speakers who read Japanese newspaper articles word by word, presented via rapid serial visual presentation. It forms part of the BCCWJ-Brain collection, which includes fMRI, MEG, and EEG data from separate participant groups exposed to the same stimuli, enabling cross-modal comparisons of language processing at high spatial and temporal resolution. T1-weighted structural images were also acquired for source localization purposes.
datasets.authors: Yushi Sugimoto, Masayuki Asahara, Hyeonjeong Jeong, Akitake Kanno, Masatoshi Koizumi, Yohei Oseki

datasets.name: BCCWJ-EEG
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings from 41 Japanese native speakers who read Japanese newspaper articles from the Balanced Corpus of Contemporary Written Japanese (BCCWJ), presented word by word via rapid serial visual presentation. It is part of the BCCWJ-Brain collection, which also includes fMRI and MEG datasets acquired from separate participant groups using the same stimuli, enabling cross-modal comparisons of language processing with complementary spatial and temporal resolution.
datasets.authors: Yushi Sugimoto, Masayuki Asahara, Hyeonjeong Jeong, Akitake Kanno, Masatoshi Koizumi, Yohei Oseki

datasets.name: Hierarchical Priors in Perceptual Uncertainty and Psychosis Proneness - A Random-Dot Kinematogram task with low- and high-level priors
datasets.description: This dataset contains cue-locked EEG recordings and behavioral event annotations from 43 healthy adults performing a random-dot kinematogram (RDK) task designed to dissociate low-level and high-level hierarchical priors during perceptual decision-making. The study examines how such priors bias behavior via signal detection theory and generalized drift-diffusion modeling, and how they modulate occipital oscillatory and aperiodic EEG activity. Participants also completed questionnaires assessing psychosis proneness and psychological flexibility traits.

datasets.name: A COVID-19 survivors and close contacts EEG dataset
datasets.description: This dataset comprises resting-state EEG recordings from 173 individuals, including 86 healthy close contacts and 87 COVID-19 survivors, collected at the Cuban Neuroscience Center. The dataset was designed to characterize EEG signatures associated with COVID-19 survival and to compare them with a Cuban EEG normative database. Recordings were obtained using a standard 10-20 montage under resting conditions with eyes closed and alternating eyes open/closed periods.
